name: Masculine / Feminine
description: Two-gender system distinguishing masculine and feminine. Common in Romance languages (Spanish, French, Italian).

name: Masculine / Feminine / Neuter
description: Three-gender system distinguishing masculine, feminine, and neuter. Common in Indo-European languages (German, Latin, Russian).

name: Animate / Inanimate
description: Noun class system based on animacy. Common in Algonquian languages and in some Slavic gender subsystems.

name: Common / Neuter
description: Two-gender system merging masculine and feminine into "common" vs neuter. Found in Swedish, Danish, Dutch.

name: Singular / Plural
description: Two-number system: one vs more than one. The most common number system worldwide.

name: Singular / Dual / Plural
description: Three-number system with a separate form for exactly two. Found in Arabic, Ancient Greek, and Slovene.

name: Singular / Plural / Collective
description: Number system including a collective form referring to a group as an undifferentiated whole (e.g. "cattle").

name: NOM / ACC / GEN / DAT (basic accusative)
description: Four-case nominative-accusative system: subject, object, possessor, recipient. Core of German and Russian inflection.

name: ABS / ERG / GEN / DAT (basic ergative)
description: Four-case ergative-absolutive system: absolutive marks the subject of intransitive verbs and the object of transitive verbs; ergative marks the agent of a transitive verb.

name: Latin-style (NOM/ACC/GEN/DAT/ABL/LOC/INSTR)
description: Rich seven-case system covering spatial, instrumental, and grammatical roles. Found in Latin, Sanskrit, and many Slavic languages.

name: Present / Past
description: Two-tense system (present vs past). Future is often expressed analytically with an auxiliary. Found in English.

name: Present / Past / Future
description: Three-tense system. Found in Latin, French, Spanish, and many other Romance and Slavic languages.

name: Non-future / Future
description: Two-tense system distinguishing future from everything else. Common in Australian Aboriginal languages and some Papuan languages.

name: Perfective / Imperfective
description: Binary aspectual distinction: completed whole action vs ongoing or repeated action. Core to Slavic verb morphology.

name: Progressive / Habitual / Perfect
description: Three-way aspectual system: ongoing action, customary action, completed action with current relevance.

name: 1st / 2nd / 3rd
description: Standard three-way person distinction: speaker, addressee, other.

name: 1 INCL / 1 EXCL / 2 / 3
description: Four-way person distinction including clusivity: first person inclusive includes the addressee, exclusive does not. Common in Austronesian and Dravidian languages.

name: Indicative / Subjunctive / Imperative
description: Three-mood system distinguishing factual statement, counterfactual / volitional, and direct command.

name: Indicative / Optative / Imperative
description: Three-mood system including an optative for wishes and hopes. Found in Ancient Greek and Sanskrit.

name: Active / Passive
description: Two-voice system contrasting the agent-as-subject active with the patient-as-subject passive.

name: Active / Middle / Passive
description: Three-voice system with a middle voice for reflexive / self-affecting actions. Found in Ancient Greek and Sanskrit.

name: Definite / Indefinite
description: Two-way definiteness system typically marked on the noun (e.g. Arabic, Swedish, Romanian) rather than with articles.
